newsitem.title: FRANCE: Six climbers die on Mont Blanc, toll this week 17. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Six climbers die on Mont Blanc, toll this week 17. [CORRECTED 13:10 GMT]

text.p: Six climbers have died on Mont Blanc in three separate accidents, raising the death toll on Europe's highest peak to 17 in recent days, French gendarmes said on Wednesday.

Four climbers fell to their deaths on Wednesday and rescue workers in a helicopter found the frozen bodies of a British and a Dutch climber missing since July 10. The nationalities of the four were not immediately known.
Police said two of the climbers died in a fall at 3 a.m. (0100 GMT) on the Couturier corridor on the Aiguille Verte side of the Mont Blanc massif. A third climber survived the fall.
Two other climbers fell to their deaths in the Tacul area of Mont Blanc about four hours later.
Eleven other people had died on the mountain since Saturday.

Rescue workers said fine weather has led to a surge in the number of climbers visiting the 4,807 metre (15,623 ft) Mont Blanc (corrects height). Some climbers, trying to get away from the crowds, were taking tougher or riskier routes.
